subject: Post-call: infra qualification — identity, keys, and long-term logging
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finexa.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@finexa.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: infra qualification — identity, keys, and long-term logging

Hi Elena / Marcus — thanks for your time this morning. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the deployment-path decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap of constraints you shared:
- SSO: SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated flows and SCIM provisioning required; strict session timeouts and attribute mappings.
- Keys: customer-managed keys required; preference for HSM-backed KMS where key material never leaves your control.
- Logging: audit logs (request/response metadata, auth events) retained for regulatory purposes — 7 years retention target. Logs must be exportable to your SIEM (S3/syslog) and encrypted at rest.
- Network: IP allowlisting and the ability to peer with your VPC or run in your environment for egress control.
- Data residency: primary US region; some project teams may require a private VPC.

High-level assessment (what we discussed):
- Hosted API (out-of-the-box): fastest to go-live, but cannot meet HSM-backed KMS or strict private-network requirements today.
- Dedicated capacity: available for reserved pools; can provide stronger isolation and some KMS integrations, but still limited for "no-key-export" HSM guarantees unless deployed into your cloud account with BYOK/HSM.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): best fit for the full control case — supports customer-managed HSM KMS, VPC peering, and long-term log retention inside your environment.

Requested next items (what we need from Finexa):
1) Security questionnaire (SOC2, pen test) — I attached our Redwood_Security_Pack_v2.pdf.
2) Confirmation of absolute requirements (e.g., is HSM mandatory vs. cloud-managed KMS acceptable?)
3) Network checklist: do you prefer peering, VPN, or on-prem appliance?
4) Timeline / decision owner + target go-live window.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical sync with your infra/security engineers to map a concrete architecture and walk through KMS/HSM options. We propose Thu, 06 May 2027 at 10:00 PT — does that work?

I'll leave Dev on thread for technical follow-up. Thanks — looking forward to narrowing this down.

— Hannah

From: Elena Morales <elena@finexa.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@finexa.com>, security@finexa.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: infra qualification — identity, keys, and long-term logging

Hi Hannah — thanks for the detailed recap. A couple clarifications from our security and infra teams: 

- KMS/HSM: HSM-backed keys are a hard requirement for our regulated lines of business. We cannot accept any solution where key material could be exported or controlled by a third party. If you have a BYOK + HSM workflow that runs in our cloud account (or supports on-prem HSM), please outline it.
- Logs: 7 years retention is correct for our audit needs. Logs must be exportable to our central S3 bucket (encrypted using our keys) and we need the ability to stream audit events to our SIEM.
- Model isolation / data handling: we need confirmation that inference workloads for our tenant will not be mixed with other customers at the model/cache level. If any caching/prefix reuse exists, how is PII scrubbed?

I've attached our Finexa_Security_RQ_0428.pdf with specific questionnaire items. For the technical sync, Thu 06 May 10:00 PT works for us — Marcus (IT Ops) and I will be there.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Security Validation
Finexa Health
elena@finexa.com

Attachment: Finexa_Security_RQ_0428.pdf (security questionnaire)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finexa.com>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@finexa.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: infra qualification — identity, keys, and long-term logging

Thanks Elena — good questions. A quick technical breakdown and what's feasible today vs what we'd recommend: 

1) HSM / CMEK options:
- Private (VPC / on-prem): we can deploy the Redwood Private control plane into your VPC or on-prem environment. In that model, you control the KMS/HSM and Redwood never has access to key material — meets the "no key export" requirement.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): we can support BYOK where keys reside in your cloud KMS (e.g., CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM). For an absolute HSM non-export guarantee, the recommended pattern is to deploy Dedicated nodes into a customer-managed cloud account where the HSM lives. That requires some networking setup and IAM work, but is lower lift than full on-prem.
- Hosted: cannot meet HSM non-export requirement today.

2) Log retention & export:
- For Private deployments we can write logs directly to your S3 bucket or streaming endpoint, encrypted under your keys, and retain per your retention policy (7 years).
- For Dedicated in our account, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM but long-term retention on your side requires shipping logs out; we can provide automated export pipelines.

3) Model isolation / cache concerns:
- Private provides tenant-dedicated runtime with no cross-tenant KV cache sharing.
- Dedicated provides strong process-level isolation; we can enforce per-tenant cache keys and zero-prefix-reuse policies for Finexa workloads. We'll document the guarantees and provide a small evaluation run to demonstrate isolation and PII handling.

Action items from Redwood (what we'll deliver before the sync):
- Short write-up: recommended architectures (Private vs Dedicated runbook) and the trade-offs (attached: KMS-HSM-integration-notes.md).
- Network checklist for peering / private deployment.
- Example IAM policies and CloudHSM configuration notes.

If you confirm that HSM non-export is non-negotiable, we'll prepare a Private deployment proposal and a timeline for a POC (2–4 weeks to provision + testing, estimate). If you'd prefer to start with Dedicated in your cloud account to shorten time-to-prod, we can scope that approach and list the remaining risks.

Hannah / Aditya — should we propose the 06 May 10:00 PT invite as an "infra deep-dive" with a short agenda?

— Dev
